list.name: solar
list.label: Solar series
list.query: SELECT so.slug || '/' || se.metric FROM core_series se JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id WHERE so.kind = 'solar' AND se.unit = 'W' ORDER BY 1

list.name: grid

list.query: SELECT so.slug || '/' || se.metric FROM core_series se JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id WHERE so.kind = 'grid' AND se.unit = 'W' ORDER BY 1

list.name: series
list.label: All series
list.query: SELECT so.slug || '/' || se.metric FROM core_series se JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id ORDER BY so.kind, 1

panels.title: Solar now
panels.description: Latest production sample, only if it arrived in the last 10 minutes. Blank means unknown, never zero.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT s.value AS "Solar now"
FROM core_sample s
JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
WHERE so.slug || '/' || se.metric = '$solar'
  AND s.ts >= datetime('now', '-10 minutes')
ORDER BY s.ts DESC
LIMIT 1

panels.title: House load (est.)
panels.description: Solar production + grid demand, from each source's most recent sample. An estimate: the two meters report at different rates (60s vs ~8s), so the two readings are near-simultaneous, not simultaneous. Blank unless both are fresh.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT
  (SELECT s.value FROM core_sample s
     JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
     JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
    WHERE so.slug || '/' || se.metric = '$solar'
      AND s.ts >= datetime('now', '-10 minutes')
    ORDER BY s.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  +
  (SELECT s.value FROM core_sample s
     JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
     JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
    WHERE so.slug || '/' || se.metric = '$grid'
      AND s.ts >= datetime('now', '-10 minutes')
    ORDER BY s.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  AS "House load"
targets.queryText:

     JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
    WHERE so.slug || '/' || se.metric = '$solar'
      AND s.ts >= datetime('now', '-10 minutes')
    ORDER BY s.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  +
  (SELECT s.value FROM core_sample s
     JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
     JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
    WHERE so.slug || '/' || se.metric = '$grid'
      AND s.ts >= datetime('now', '-10 minutes')
    ORDER BY s.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  AS "House load"

panels.title: Solar today
panels.description: Energy since local midnight, integrated from each sample's value x duration. Only observed time counts — a collector outage lowers this number rather than filling it in.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT SUM(s.value * s.duration_s) / 3600000.0 AS "Solar today"
FROM core_sample s
JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
WHERE so.slug || '/' || se.metric = '$solar'
  AND s.ts >= datetime(datetime('now', 'localtime', 'start of day'), 'utc')

panels.title: Imported today
panels.description: Grid energy drawn since local midnight (positive demand only).

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.value > 0 THEN s.value * s.duration_s ELSE 0 END) / 3600000.0 AS "Imported today"
FROM core_sample s
JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
WHERE so.slug || '/' || se.metric = '$grid'
  AND s.ts >= datetime(datetime('now', 'localtime', 'start of day'), 'utc')

panels.title: Exported today

FROM core_sample s
JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
WHERE so.slug || '/' || se.metric = '$grid'
  AND s.ts >= datetime(datetime('now', 'localtime', 'start of day'), 'utc')

panels.title: Power — solar production vs. grid demand
panels.description: Both series are watts, so they share one axis. Every point is a stored sample; nothing is interpolated. A break in a line is a real gap in the data, not zero output.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', s.ts) AS INTEGER) AS time,
       s.value AS "Solar production"
FROM core_sample s
JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
WHERE so.slug || '/' || se.metric = '$solar'
  AND s.ts >= datetime($__from / 1000, 'unixepoch')
  AND s.ts <  datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
ORDER BY s.ts
